history.dynasty: BAPS (Bochasanwasi Shri Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha)
history.summary: A modern temple complex built by the BAPS Swaminarayan organisation at the turn of the 21st century; it has no ancient or legendary history and sources disagree on its exact construction year (described as late 20th century by some, beginning of the 21st century by others — verify). Set in landscaped gardens with fountains, the temple is known for its intricate stone carvings, paintings and murals depicting Hindu mythology. The central shrine (Hari Mandapam) houses a gold-leafed idol of Lord Swaminarayan. Photography is not permitted inside the complex; the temple is reportedly closed on Mondays (verify).

name: Akshardham (Swaminarayan) Temple
town_description: Jaipur, the capital of Rajasthan, is the 'Pink City' — founded in 1727 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, its rose-hued walled old city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the historic heart of Kachwaha Rajput culture, home to the City Palace, Hawa Mahal and Jantar Mantar. The temple stands in Vaishali Nagar, a western residential locality of the city near Ajmer Road.

travel.airport: Jaipur International Airport, roughly 12 km away (verify).
travel.railway: Jaipur Junction railway station, roughly 7 km away (verify).
travel.road: Vaishali Nagar (Chitrakoot), off Ajmer Road; reachable by city bus, auto-rickshaw and taxi.

visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported as 7:30 AM-10:00 AM and 4:00 PM-7:00 PM with Monday closed — verify, sources conflict.
